page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-180 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration powered by fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9B14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 90 physical cores yielding 180 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. The hardware configuration includes 720 GB of memory, maintaining a 4 GB per vCPU ratio. Dedicated CPU caches deliver 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by vector and instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and VAES.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-decile throughput in parallel compute and memory subsystems. In multi-threaded evaluations, the platform achieved a top-tier stress-ng score of 277,209.33 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 22,069.0, driven by its 180-thread capacity. Computational compilation tests via Clang registered 76,010.0, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Memory operations deliver up to 13,454.22 GB/sec for small cached reads and 169.03 GB/sec in large-block writes. Key-value operations showed high throughput, recording 211.43 million Redis SET operations per second.

The instance does not bundle local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, meaning persistent disk volumes and network interfaces must be attached separately based on deployment architecture. For compute-dense workloads, the instance offers strong resource efficiency by consolidating wide parallel threads and 720 GB of RAM into a single non-accelerated node, avoiding GPU operational premiums for CPU-based inference and large-scale batch tasks.

Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-180 fits large multi-threaded application suites, such as continuous integration build pipelines, CPU-based large language model inference, in-memory caching systems, and enterprise data processing workflows.
